testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both spring force and air pressure at the same time will damage the brakes.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, you should:

options.text: Be especially careful because the brakes may fail.

questions.explanation: Do not press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both forces at once will damage the brakes.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: The brakes will not work as well without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.explanation: When a tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, jackknifing is less likely to happen. The driver can still control the steering. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing out.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, a leak in one system:

options.text: Always means both systems are leaking.
May not affect the other system.
Will also affect the other system.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect the other system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other one.

questions.question: How is the parking brake released?

options.text: By tapping the brake pedal three times
By pushing in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: By pushing in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: The parking brake is controlled by a knob. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release the brakes.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks, but each has its own hoses and lines.
Both systems use the same lines and hoses.
One system is main, and a second one is ready if the first fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems with their own air tanks, hoses, and lines. Both systems share the same brake controls.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.
Safely pull off the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and stop.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on, stop the vehicle right away and park it safely. This warning means there is a problem in the air brake system that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system use?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles use different numbers and sizes of air tanks in their air brake systems.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you must wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of ____ in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.explanation: Wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both systems before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system.

questions.question: In cold weather, an alcohol evaporator should be checked and filled:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from forming in an air brake system. Check and refill it every day in cold weather.

questions.question: What causes brake fading?

options.text: Brakes are not used often enough.

questions.explanation: Using brakes too much causes them to overheat. When brakes overheat, they become less effective. This is called brake fading.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To find out if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: While driving, what holds spring brakes in place?
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle.
To stop the vehicle during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Cannot be used with air brakes.
Should be used on dry pavement.
Should only be used if all axles have ABS.

questions.explanation: ABS works with air braking systems. ABS helps you maintain control and prevents wheels from locking up during hard braking on slippery surfaces. ABS provides benefits even if only one axle has it.

questions.question: What should you do with water and compressor oil in an air brake system?

options.text: They are necessary for proper brake function.
Add them if they are low.

questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open the air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. If leakage is faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: How should you set a front brake limiting valve for normal stopping power?

options.text: Keep it at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some vehicles made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Studies show this valve does not actually help. Always leave it in the "normal" position.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too much lets air out faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure drops too low, the brakes will stop working.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after pushing the pedal.
The distance between the brake pedal's resting position and the floor.
The amount of air pressure needed to stop a vehicle.
How faded the brakes have become.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after pushing the pedal.
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through air lines to the brakes. There is a delay of at least half a second between pushing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work. This delay is called brake lag. Hydraulic brakes work instantly when the pedal is pressed.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds how many feet to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate allowed for a single vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure activates a switch that:

options.text: Turns on the low pressure warning light
Turns off the low pressure warning light

questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air pressure moves an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light is red. It may also have a buzzer that sounds to alert the driver.

questions.question: Friction in a brake drum happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Push against the inside of the drum

questions.correctAnswerText: Push against the inside of the drum
questions.explanation: Friction forms when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.
